gemma4_verdict: google/gemma-4-31B-it is natively multimodal (image, video, audio, plus text) in a single decoder-only transformer with a ~550M-parameter vision encoder supporting variable aspect ratios and a configurable token budget per image (70 to 1120 tokens), letting you trade speed for OCR/document fidelity. Its image stack explicitly targets academic-document tasks: document/PDF parsing, chart comprehension, table reading, multilingual OCR, handwriting, and screen/UI understanding. Reported vision benchmarks for the 31B IT are strong: MMMU-Pro 76.9% (up from 49.7% on Gemma 3), MATH-Vision 85.6% (nearly double Gemma 3's 46.0%), and OmniDocBench 1.5 average edit distance 0.131 (lower is better; roughly a two-thirds error reduction vs the prior generation). DocVQA/ChartQA/InfoVQA are described as competitive (the 26B sibling scores ~94.9 DocVQA, ~88 InfoVQA; exact 31B per-benchmark figures were not cleanly broken out in indexed sources [uncertain]). Practically this means Gemma 4 31B can read dense figure captions, axes labels, and result tables directly from a rendered PDF page without a separate OCR stage. Multimodal works in llama.cpp via a separate mmproj projector GGUF and via MLX (mlx-vlm) on Apple Silicon. Apache 2.0 license, 256K context. This is a decisive structural advantage for Labmate's figure-heavy paper-reading workload because it is the orchestrator brain itself, not a bolt-on.
qwen3_verdict: Qwen/Qwen3-32B (the model named in CLAUDE.md as the specialist worker) is TEXT-ONLY. Vision is a separate model line: Qwen3-VL (dense 2B/4B/8B/32B and MoE 30B-A3B/235B-A22B, released 2025-10-21), and the newer Qwen3.6 line (Apr 2026) which is natively multimodal but ships only as 27B dense and 35B-A3B MoE — there is no Qwen3.6 dense 32B. So out of the box, Qwen3-32B cannot read paper figures/charts/tables at all; it can only consume text that some upstream stage has already extracted. The practical substitute at the same parameter scale is Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct (~33B params, Apache 2.0), which is an outstanding document model: DocVQA test ~96.5-96.9%, OCRBench 875, MMMU 76.0, MathVista-mini 83.8, MathVision 63.4, AI2D 89.5, CharXiv description 90.5 / reasoning ~66.2, ScreenSpot 95.8, MMLongBench-Doc 54.6%. It outperforms the larger Qwen2.5-VL-72B on ~15 benchmarks including OCRBench, AI2D, MathVision, and MMMU-Pro, supports 39 OCR languages and 256K context. It can even run text-only in vLLM (--limit-mm-per-prompt.image 0 --limit-mm-per-prompt.video 0) to reclaim KV-cache memory. The catch: it is a different model from Qwen3-32B, so adopting it means swapping the worker model (or running a second model), not flipping a flag on Qwen3-32B.
benchmarks: Gemma 4 31B IT (vision): MMMU-Pro 76.9%, MATH-Vision 85.6%, OmniDocBench 1.5 edit distance 0.131 (lower better); DocVQA/ChartQA/InfoVQA reported competitive (26B sibling ~94.9 DocVQA / ~88 InfoVQA) [uncertain on exact 31B figures]. Qwen3-32B (text-only): no vision benchmarks — n/a. Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct (substitute): DocVQA ~96.5-96.9%, OCRBench 875, MMMU 76.0, MathVista-mini 83.8, MathVision 63.4, AI2D 89.5, CharXiv-D 90.5 / reasoning ~66.2, MMLongBench-Doc 54.6%. Head-to-head document QA slightly favors Qwen3-VL-32B (DocVQA/OCRBench), while Gemma 4 31B leads on multimodal math/reasoning over images (MATH-Vision 85.6% vs Qwen3-VL-32B 63.4%) and matches it on MMMU (76.9 MMMU-Pro region vs 76.0 MMMU).
factual_accuracy: For document grounding, native vision lowers confabulation risk versus an OCR-then-text pipeline, because the model sees axes, legends, and table cells directly rather than trusting a lossy text dump that can silently drop or transpose numbers — a first-class concern for scientific work. Gemma 4 31B's strong MATH-Vision (85.6%) and OmniDocBench (0.131 edit distance) indicate reliable extraction of numeric/figure content. Qwen3-VL-32B's DocVQA ~96.5% and OCRBench 875 indicate very low text-recognition error. A pure Qwen3-32B + external-OCR path inherits the OCR engine's error rate on multi-column layouts, math, and complex tables, which is the dominant failure mode for academic PDFs. No SimpleQA/TruthfulQA figures specific to the vision-document setting were found [uncertain].
inference_speed: Vision adds cost on two axes: the vision-encoder forward pass plus the image-token expansion in the context (Gemma 4: 70-1120 tokens per image, tunable; Qwen3-VL uses dynamic-resolution tokenization). On non-CUDA, Gemma 4 multimodal runs through llama.cpp (Metal/ROCm/Vulkan/SYCL) with an mmproj projector and through MLX (mlx-vlm) on Apple Silicon. Per-image latency depends heavily on the chosen token budget — caption-grade budgets keep loops interactive, dense-OCR budgets are slower. No measured tokens/sec figures for 31B vision on a specific 32GB non-CUDA GPU were found [uncertain]; treat throughput as encoder-overhead-plus-prefill bound rather than pure decode bound.
multimodal_support: Gemma 4 31B: native image + video + audio, single decoder-only transformer, ~550M vision encoder, variable aspect ratio, tunable per-image token budget (70-1120), explicit document/PDF parsing + chart + table + multilingual OCR capability. Qwen3-32B: TEXT-ONLY (confirmed) — no vision encoder. The Qwen vision option is the separate Qwen3-VL-32B (image + video, dynamic resolution, 256K context) or the newer Qwen3.6-27B dense (natively multimodal, but 27B not 32B). For Labmate's literal model pair (gemma-4-31B-it vs Qwen3-32B), this dimension is a hard win for Gemma: one model can read papers as rendered pages; the other cannot see at all.
context_window: Gemma 4 31B: 256K nominal context (hybrid local-sliding + global attention with proportional RoPE); long-context evals reported via MRCR v2 8-needle 128k [exact effective-window threshold not surfaced, uncertain]. Important for vision: a full paper rendered as page images consumes far more tokens than its text, so a large window is functionally required for figure-heavy reading. Qwen3-VL-32B: 256K native, expandable to ~1M, with near-perfect needle-in-haystack on the flagship and MMLongBench-Doc 54.6% at up to 256K — purpose-built for hundreds of document pages. Qwen3-32B (text-only): 256K-class context but irrelevant here since it cannot ingest the figures in the first place. A single paper is ~8k-20k text tokens; with page images or a multi-paper literature session, 32K+ is easily exceeded, so both multimodal options' 256K windows are valuable.
non_cuda_support: Gemma 4 31B multimodal on non-CUDA is well supported: llama.cpp (Metal on Apple Silicon, ROCm/HIPBLAS on AMD, Vulkan, SYCL on Intel) using the language GGUF PLUS a matching mmproj projector GGUF — without the projector the .gguf is text-only and rejects images. Official GGUFs from ggml-org and Unsloth (unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF), plus a QAT w4a16 build. MLX path via mlx-vlm gives full multimodal on Apple Silicon. Fit on 32GB non-CUDA VRAM: the 31B at Q4_K_M is ~18-22GB for weights, leaving room for the vision encoder + KV cache within 32GB on a single device — confirmed-class hardware includes AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24GB, tight), Radeon Pro W7800 (32GB), and Apple M-series with 32GB+ unified memory; a 24GB card is workable but headroom for large image-token budgets + long context is better at 32GB. Qwen3-VL-32B also has official GGUF (Qwen/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-GGUF, mix-precision LM+vision) and AWQ builds; at 4-bit it is ~18-22GB and likewise fits 32GB with room for KV cache. Build complexity: use llama.cpp master (tagged releases lag Metal/ROCm fixes); on ROCm build with -DGGML_HIPBLAS=ON.
over_refusal_risk: Not a vision-specific dimension; no XSTest or refusal data tied to the multimodal/document-reading setting was found for either model [uncertain]. General expectation: reading and discussing figures/tables from legitimately published papers is low-risk content; refusal behavior here is governed by the same safety tuning as text and is not materially changed by the image modality. Defer detailed refusal analysis to the dedicated over-refusal research item.
ecosystem_toolchain: Gemma 4 31B vision: day-one llama.cpp support (GGUF + mmproj), Ollama, LM Studio, MLX/mlx-vlm, Unsloth, vLLM. In vLLM the Gemma 4 tool-call parser flag is gemma4 (per project CLAUDE.md rule 6), and multimodal serving is supported. Strong, well-documented HF model cards (google/, ggml-org/, unsloth/). Qwen3-VL-32B: GGUF (official + QuantTrio/Mungert), AWQ (QuantTrio/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-AWQ), FP16; runs on vLLM (Qwen3-VL recipe, hermes-style tool parser), llama.cpp/Ollama, LM Studio, Unsloth (with how-to-run docs). Both ecosystems are mature; Gemma 4's advantage for Labmate is that vision lives in the same orchestrator model and shares the existing vLLM gemma4 tool-call path, whereas a Qwen vision capability requires standing up a second model line.
labmate_relevance: HIGH. Labmate's core jobs are academic paper reading, critique/review, and literature synthesis. Modern papers carry load-bearing information in figures, result tables, plots, and architecture diagrams that text extraction frequently mangles or omits (multi-column layouts, math, embedded charts). The ability of the orchestrator brain to read a rendered page directly removes a whole brittle OCR/figure-extraction stage and reduces numeric confabulation — directly improving the quality of the primary task.
recommendation: For the figure/chart/table-heavy paper-reading dimension, use Gemma 4 31B as the orchestrator brain: it is natively multimodal, so a single model both drives the loop and reads rendered PDF pages, and it leads on multimodal reasoning over images (MATH-Vision 85.6%, MMMU-Pro 76.9%) which matters for interpreting results figures and method diagrams. Qwen3-32B should NOT be the model for this dimension — it is text-only and would force an OCR/figure-extraction preprocessing pipeline (e.g. a VLM-OCR pass or tools like PDFFigures 2.0 / OmniDocBench-style parsers feeding text into Qwen), adding latency, a failure surface, and numeric-extraction errors. If Labmate wants Qwen-family vision, the substitute is Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct (slightly stronger on pure DocVQA/OCRBench, ~96.5% / 875), but that is a separate model, not Qwen3-32B, and would run as a dedicated vision worker. Recommended model-switching strategy: Gemma 4 31B as the default brain that natively reads paper pages; optionally route the most OCR-intensive document-digitization subtasks (dense scanned tables, low-quality scans) to Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct as a specialist vision worker, while keeping Qwen3-32B (text-only) for pure-text reasoning/coding tasks where vision is irrelevant. Both Gemma 4 31B (Q4_K_M + mmproj) and Qwen3-VL-32B (4-bit AWQ/GGUF) fit within 32GB non-CUDA VRAM, so the constraint does not force the decision.
